ext_p2p.a_bank_account_a_wallet_handle: A bank account, a wallet handle, a PayPal address — whatever you want a buyer to pay to.
ext_p2p.a_dispute_does_not_close_the: A dispute does not close the conversation, and the messages you send after opening one are read alongside everything else. New detail belongs there rather than in an email nobody handling the case will see.
ext_p2p.a_dispute_is_not_a_complaint: A dispute is not a complaint form. It freezes real money and puts a person on it, which is why it is worth knowing what it does before you need one.
ext_p2p.a_five_star_seller_who_takes: A five-star seller who takes forty minutes to release is a worse trade than a four-star seller who takes fifty seconds, and a row of stars cannot tell you that. Release time is the number that costs you something when you get it wrong, which is why it is on the line and a rating is not.
ext_p2p.a_shape_means_every_trader_on_this_metho: Fixed fields mean every trader using this method supplies the same things, and every buyer reads the same rows. It is also what keeps one method from appearing in the marketplace filter a hundred times over.
ext_p2p.a_taker_who_hasnt_paid_by: How long a taker gets to pay. After it you can cancel whenever you like — they can still pay until you do — and your funds come back to this offer.
ext_p2p.a_timeline_a_single_bar_represents: A timeline. A single bar represents the buyer's payment window, which starts when the trade opens and escrow locks, and ends at zero. It carries no scale because its length is set by each offer. At zero the timeline forks, and neither branch is a countdown: if the buyer confirmed in time the clock is finished and there is no clock on the seller afterwards; if nobody confirmed, the trade simply carries on — the buyer can still pay, and the seller can cancel from that point whenever they choose.
ext_p2p.a_trade_has_two_halves_and: A trade has two halves and they move in completely different ways. Almost every problem on this platform comes from not knowing which half is which.
ext_p2p.a_trade_is_still_open_on: A trade is still open on this offer, so the server will refuse to save any change until it finishes or is cancelled.
ext_p2p.a_trade_room_is_private_to: A trade room is private to the two people in it — the payment details and the chat are only ever shown to the buyer and the seller.

ext_p2p.there_is_a_fourth_figure_and_which: There is a fourth figure, and which one you see depends on which side you are on. Selling to somebody, the chip under their name is their payment time — how long they usually take to confirm payment after a trade opens, averaged the same way over their last ten trades. That is the figure a late payment costs you, and it is why the payment window running out does not end the trade.
ext_p2p.there_is_no_fourth_exit_no: Nothing said in the chat is a fourth exit — which is why “release it and I'll sort it out with you after” is always a bad trade. The only hand other than the two of yours that can reach escrow is an administrator resolving or cancelling the trade from the admin side, and that is recorded against their account.
ext_p2p.there_is_one_clock_on_a: There is one clock on a trade and it is always the buyer's. It is counting the window the offer gave them to send the money and say so — commonly fifteen minutes to an hour, and you can see it before you commit to anything. What it is not is a deadline that ends the trade: the window running out cancels nothing by itself.

ext_staking.onchain_status_active_hint: Delegated and earning what the network pays.
ext_staking.onchain_status_unstake_requested_hint: Queued for the next exit batch. Rewards stopped at the request.
ext_staking.onchain_status_unbonding_hint: The network is releasing your coins.
ext_staking.onchain_status_returning_hint: Settled; the coins are on their way to your deposit address.
ext_staking.onchain_status_refunded_hint: The coins could not be moved; the full amount was returned to your balance.
ext_staking.onchain_unstake_warning: An exit waits for the network’s unbonding and cannot be cancelled once accepted. Rewards stop at the request. Your {symbol} is credited when it lands back in your own deposit address.
ext_staking.onchain_shares_worth_note: All {held} shares are worth about {value} {symbol} at today’s price; the exit settles at that price or the price when the coins are released, whichever is lower.
ext_staking.onchain_reward_shares_note: That is the share count worth about {value} {symbol} — the rewards this position has earned so far. Your original stake keeps earning; only this part leaves.
ext_staking.onchain_pool_intro: Delegated on the network from a wallet this platform holds. The reward is what the network pays, observed on-chain, minus a stated commission.
ext_staking.onchain_intake_paused: New stakes into this pool are paused. Positions already open continue, and exits are unaffected.
ext_staking.onchain_fact_paid_out_hint: what the network paid this pool, after commission — history, not a rate
ext_staking.onchain_disclosure_caption: Generated from this pool’s records. Your stake is placed against this exact version.
ext_staking.onchain_stake_from_wallet: From your {symbol} ecosystem wallet. The coins move from your own deposit address.
ext_staking.onchain_stake_footnote: Nothing is fixed or guaranteed. An exit waits for the network’s unbonding and cannot be cancelled. Your coins are credited back when they land in your own address.
ext_staking.onchain_disclosure_read_failed: The disclosure could not be read.
ext_staking.onchain_quote_failed: The stake could not be quoted.
ext_staking.onchain_row_bunker: Lido bunker mode: exits are slower than usual
ext_staking.guide_onchain_intro: Some pools delegate your coins on the network itself. They work differently from the fixed-rate pools this guide describes, and each pool page says which kind it is.
ext_staking.guide_onchain_no_rate_body: You receive what the network paid, minus the commission stated on the pool page. The pool shows what it observed over the last 30 days; that is history, not a forecast, and it can be zero.
ext_staking.guide_onchain_no_lock_lead: No lock and no early exit.
ext_staking.guide_onchain_no_lock_body: You can ask to exit at any time, and the exit then waits for the network's unbonding period. The wait is an estimate and the request cannot be cancelled.
ext_staking.guide_onchain_coins_move_body: A stake takes the coins from your own deposit address on this platform to a staking wallet this platform holds, and delegates them from there. They come back to your address when an exit is released.
ext_staking.guide_onchain_shares_body: Your position is a share of the pool. Rewards raise the value of every share; a validator penalty on the network lowers it for every holder, including you.
ext_staking.guide_onchain_disclosure_body: Every on-chain pool page is generated from the pool's records and versioned. A stake is placed against the version you read, with five acknowledgements this platform keeps on file.
ext_staking.guide_onchain_what_to_expect: What to expect after you stake
ext_staking.guide_onchain_rewards: None of the above applies to an on-chain pool. There is no distribution schedule and no auto-compound setting: the network pays whatever it pays, the platform observes it on chain each epoch, and it raises the value of every holder's shares as it arrives. There is nothing to claim, because the rewards are not a balance this platform is holding for you — they are already yours, inside the pool, and they come back as coins when you unstake. To take only the rewards out, unstake the part of your position they represent; the rest keeps earning.
ext_staking.guide_onchain_risks: In an on-chain pool the reward is whatever the network pays, and it can be zero. A validator penalty on the network reduces the pool's value for every holder. An exit waits for the network's unbonding period, which is an estimate, and cannot be cancelled once requested. While staked, your coins are held in a wallet this platform controls and are not insured.
ext_staking.guide_onchain_state_delegating_desc: while the coins move and the network activates them.
ext_staking.guide_onchain_state_staked_desc: once the network has accepted the delegation.
ext_staking.guide_onchain_state_exit_requested_desc: from the moment you ask to leave.
ext_staking.guide_onchain_state_unbonding_desc: with the date the coins are expected back.
ext_staking.guide_onchain_state_returned_desc: once they are in your address.
ext_staking.guide_onchain_state_failed_desc: if the stake could not be placed. It is refunded, with the reason.

Withdrawals are usually gated on identity verification, so we start there. If you are already verified this takes a moment and we move on.
Next, where the money you can withdraw actually lives.
support_assistant.workflows.first_withdrawal.steps.wallets: Now the balance itself. Only what is available can be withdrawn — anything in an open order or an earlier pending withdrawal is held, and that is the usual reason the amount you expect is not the amount offered.
support_assistant.workflows.first_withdrawal.steps.withdra: Last, the withdrawal form. I will stop on the destination field, because that is the one thing nobody can undo for you afterwards.
That is everything. Your request will appear in your transaction history with a status.
support_assistant.workflows.first_withdrawal.title: Take money out for the first time
support_assistant.workflows.join_a_token_sale.steps.offers: Everything currently raising, with what each one is selling and how far along it is. Read the terms — a token sale is not a deposit, and the value can go to zero.
Anything you buy into shows up on your transactions page.
support_assistant.workflows.join_a_token_sale.steps.transa: Your purchases and, where the sale has a release schedule, when each portion becomes available.
That is the whole picture. Release schedules are set by the project, not by us.
support_assistant.workflows.join_a_token_sale.steps.verify: Token sales are usually gated on identity verification. We start there because it is the most common reason somebody cannot take part.
support_assistant.workflows.join_a_token_sale.title: Take part in a token sale
support_assistant.workflows.place_a_store_order.steps.brow: Everything available, with its price and whether it is in stock. Add what you want to your basket as you go.
support_assistant.workflows.place_a_store_order.steps.cart: Check the quantities and the total before you go on. Orders are paid from your wallet balance, so make sure the right wallet has enough in it.
Checkout is the next step from here.
support_assistant.workflows.place_a_store_order.steps.orde: Every order you have placed, with its status and any tracking. This is the page to check before asking where something is.
If an order is stuck, quote its number and I will bring in a person.
support_assistant.workflows.place_a_store_order.title: Buy something from the store
support_assistant.workflows.recover_access.steps.resend.de: We will send the verification link again to the email address on your account.
support_assistant.workflows.recover_access.steps.sign_in.d: Once you have opened the link in that email, sign in here. If the email has not arrived after a few minutes, check the spam folder before trying again.
You are on the sign-in page. If the link still has not arrived, tell me and I will bring in a person.
support_assistant.workflows.recover_access.title: Get back into your account
support_assistant.workflows.redo_verification.steps.resubm: Your submission has been withdrawn. Because a withdrawal is recorded as a rejection, the next submission for that level opens in 24 hours — go to the verification page to check where you stand and get the right documents ready.
You are on the verification page. It shows your current status, and you can submit again once the 24 hours are up.
support_assistant.workflows.redo_verification.steps.withdr: We will withdraw the verification submission you have waiting for review. It is recorded as a rejection, so you will not be able to submit for that level again for 24 hours. Anything you have already been approved for is unaffected, and your uploaded documents are not deleted.
support_assistant.workflows.redo_verification.title: Start your verification again
support_assistant.workflows.secure_my_account.steps.notifi: Every sign-in, withdrawal and security change is recorded here. Read back through it — anything you do not recognise is worth telling us about straight away.
If you see something you did not do, tell me now and I will bring in a person immediately.
support_assistant.workflows.secure_my_account.steps.two_fa: The single biggest thing you can do is two-factor authentication. I'll show you exactly where it is and what to expect.
Now let's make sure you can see anything that happens on the account.
support_assistant.workflows.secure_my_account.title: Lock down your account
support_assistant.workflows.start_binary_trading.steps.fun: When you move off practice mode, this is the balance a real trade draws on and where to top it up.
That is everything. Practise first — there is no cost to it.
support_assistant.workflows.start_binary_trading.steps.ter: This is the walkthrough the binary screen ships with. It covers the chart, the expiry, and the practice mode — start in practice mode.
Next, where the money for a real trade comes from.
support_assistant.workflows.start_binary_trading.title: Get started with binary options
support_assistant.workflows.start_copy_trading.steps.brows: Traders you can follow, with their history. Past performance is not a promise — allocate only what you would be willing to lose on somebody else's decisions.
support_assistant.workflows.start_copy_trading.steps.subsc: Everyone you currently follow and how much is allocated to each. Pausing and stopping both live here — this is the page you want if you have changed your mind.
Stopping does not close positions that are already open. Check those separately.
support_assistant.workflows.start_copy_trading.title: Follow another trader
support_assistant.workflows.start_forex_investing.steps.in: Everything you have running and what it has returned. Results here are not guaranteed by us, whatever a plan's headline rate says.
That is where to check on it from now on.
support_assistant.workflows.start_forex_investing.steps.pl: Managed plans, each with its minimum, its term and its stated return. This is money managed on your behalf, which is a different thing from trading it yourself.
Next, where an investment is tracked.
support_assistant.workflows.start_forex_investing.title: Invest in a managed forex plan
support_assistant.workflows.start_forex_trading.steps.fund: A position needs a funded balance. Let's confirm yours first — it is the usual reason a first order is refused.
support_assistant.workflows.start_forex_trading.steps.term: Now the forex screen itself — this is the walkthrough it ships with, covering the chart, the order ticket and your open positions.
That is the terminal. Leverage magnifies losses as well as gains — start small.
support_assistant.workflows.start_forex_trading.title: Get started on the forex terminal
support_assistant.workflows.start_investing.steps.fund.des: A plan is funded from your wallet, so let's confirm what is available first.
support_assistant.workflows.start_investing.steps.plans.de: Each plan states its rate, its term and its currency. The term is a commitment — read what happens if you want out early before you commit anything.
support_assistant.workflows.start_investing.steps.plans.do: Anything you start appears in your portfolio.
support_assistant.workflows.start_investing.steps.portfoli: Everything you have running, what it has returned so far, and when each one matures.
That is where to check on it from now on.
support_assistant.workflows.start_investing.title: Put money into an investment plan
support_assistant.workflows.start_p2p_trading.steps.market: These are live offers from other people. Check the trader's completed-trade count and their terms before you commit — you are trading with a person, not with us.
Once you open a trade, funds are held in escrow until both sides are done.
support_assistant.workflows.start_p2p_trading.steps.paymen: Before your first trade you need at least one payment method saved, so the person on the other side knows how to pay you or how to be paid. Add one here.
With a method saved, you can be matched. Next, the market.
support_assistant.workflows.start_p2p_trading.steps.trades: Every trade you open lives here with its stage and its countdown. This is the page to be on while a trade is running — it is also where the dispute button is if something goes wrong.
Never release funds until you have confirmed payment arrived in your own account, not just that the other side says it has.
support_assistant.workflows.start_p2p_trading.title: Buy or sell peer-to-peer for the first time
support_assistant.workflows.start_referring.steps.programm: This is your referral link and what the programme pays. The link is the only thing that attributes a signup to you — a referral who signs up without it cannot be credited afterwards.
What each referral has earned you and whether it has been paid out yet. A reward usually has conditions attached — the referred person completing something, not merely signing up.
If a referral is missing here, that is worth a ticket — include when they signed up.
support_assistant.workflows.start_referring.title: Start earning from referrals
An order needs a funded balance in the right wallet, and that is the usual reason a first order is refused. Let's check yours before anything else.
support_assistant.workflows.start_spot_trading.steps.termi: Now the terminal itself. This is the walkthrough the trading screen ships with — the chart, the order book, and the order ticket.
That is the terminal. Nothing is placed until you press the button yourself.
support_assistant.workflows.start_spot_trading.title: Place your first trade
support_assistant.workflows.start_staking.steps.fund.descr: Staking locks tokens you already hold, so let's start with what is in your wallets and which of it is actually available.
support_assistant.workflows.start_staking.steps.fund.label: Check what I hold
support_assistant.workflows.start_staking.steps.pools.desc: Each pool has its own rate and its own lock period. The lock is the part to read carefully — your tokens are committed for that long, and leaving early may cost you.
support_assistant.workflows.start_staking.steps.pools.done: Once you have staked, your position appears on the next page.
Your stakes, what they have earned, and when each lock ends. Rewards are claimed from here.
That is the whole cycle: stake, earn, claim when the lock ends.
support_assistant.workflows.start_staking.title: Stake for the first time
support_assistant.workflows.start_swapping.steps.confirm.d: A completed swap appears in your history like any other movement. This is where to confirm what you received.
If a swap is missing here after the network has confirmed it, tell me.
support_assistant.workflows.start_swapping.steps.swap.desc: This is the walkthrough the swap screen ships with. It covers picking the two tokens, slippage, and the network fee — which is charged by the network, not by us.
support_assistant.workflows.start_swapping.steps.swap.done: Next, where to check the swap actually landed.
support_assistant.workflows.start_swapping.title: Swap one token for another
